newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to raise public rents by 50 percent.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to raise public rents by 50 percent.

text.p: Shanghai city government on Wednesday announced an increase of 50 percent in rents on public apartments, part of a plan to stimulate the housing market, the Xinmin Evening News reported.
The rates of increase will be higher for commercial offices and people living in large apartments and will be lower for retired officials and families in difficulties, it said.
The tax on purchases of apartments for foreigners -- including those from Hong Kong and Taiwan -- will be halved to 0.5 percent of the purchase price, it said.
Banks should gradually shift the focus of their loans from firms building apartments to those buying them, it said but gave no more details.
Earlier this month Shanghai started allowing residents from outside the city to obtain residence permits by purchasing apartments of a certain size in the Pudong area of the city.
